question: For which of the following fields did Marie Curie win the Nobel Prize?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Physics and Chemistry**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Marie Curie** won the Nobel Prize in both **Physics** and **Chemistry**.
 
• She was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903** for her research on radiation phenomena.
 
• She received the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911** for her discovery of the elements radium and polonium.
 
• Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields.
 
• Her pioneering work laid the foundation for future research in both physics and chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marie Curie's** research was crucial in the development of X-ray machines.
 
• She coined the term "radioactivity" and developed techniques for isolating radioactive isotopes.
 
• Curie founded the Curie Institutes in Paris and Warsaw, which remain major centers of medical research today.
 
• Despite facing significant obstacles as a woman in science during her time, Marie Curie's contributions have had a lasting impact on the fields of physics and chemistry.
 
• Her work not only advanced scientific understanding but also had practical applications in medicine, particularly in cancer treatment through radiotherapy.
